# Synthetic Scale Benchmark — Multi-day and Downstream Tools (#35)

**Evidence date:** 2026-11-09 UTC. **Data:** synthetic, fictional AIS generated by `tools/benchmark_multiday.py` (800 MMSIs, alternating stops and movement, one observation per ~2 minutes per MMSI). **Not real vessel activity and not a NOAA run.** Environment: one Linux cloud container, Python 3.13.

## Why

A full UTC day in the Houston research rectangle is about 560,000 rows (about 140,000 per six hours in the 2024-01-02/03 NOAA smokes). The previous ceilings (250,000 extracted rows, 1.5 million multi-day rows, 20,000 track-context candidates, 10,000 observations per candidate) blocked full-day extraction and the 3–7 day studies in the validation protocol.

## Results

| Measurement | 2 days × 500k rows | 7 days × 560k rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Input rows | 1,000,000 | 3,920,000 |
| `harborlens-multiday` elapsed | 20.2 s | 78.2 s |
| Peak RSS (process) | 47.0 MiB | 47.2 MiB |
| SQLite scratch peak | 153.6 MiB | 628.5 MiB |
| Scratch bytes per row | 161 | 168 |
| Cleaned CSV export | 57.9 MiB | 226.6 MiB |
| Unvalidated candidates | 8,203 | 31,249 |

On the 7-day output, `harborlens-track-context` (one synthetic polygon) took 51.1 s at 229 MiB RSS, and `harborlens-label-sample` (70 + 30 units) took 24.4 s at 1,831 MiB RSS, because it loads all cleaned rows in memory (about 470 bytes per row).

Scratch size is sampled at SQLite commits, including the rollback journal; real NOAA rows may be wider than the synthetic ones.

## Resulting ceilings (all still fail closed)

| Tool | Limit | Old | New |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `harborlens-extract-noaa-archive` | matched rows | 250,000 | 1,000,000 |
| | output MiB (default / ceiling) | 64 / 128 | 128 / 256 |
| `harborlens-multiday` | input rows | 1,500,000 | 6,000,000 |
| | SQLite scratch MiB | 1,024 | 2,048 |
| | export MiB (default / ceiling) | 256 / 512 | 1,024 / 2,048 |
| `harborlens-track-context` | cleaned rows / candidates / points per candidate | 1.5M / 20,000 / 10,000 | 6M / 100,000 / 60,000 |
| | SQLite scratch MiB / output MiB | 768 / 48 | 2,048 / 256 |
| In-memory tools (`label-sample`, `sensitivity`) | cleaned rows | none / 1.5M | 6,000,000 (about 2.8 GiB RSS) |

The multi-day manifest now records `limits` and `resources.scratch_peak_bytes`; the extraction sidecar and the single-file manifest record their limits.

## Reproduce

~~~bash
python tools/benchmark_multiday.py --rows-per-day 560000 --days 7 --workdir /tmp/hl-bench
~~~

## Still open

A real run over seven consecutive full NOAA days (`.github/workflows/noaa-week-integration.yml`, manual) must confirm these numbers before NFR-007 can be claimed for real data.

**NOT FOR NAVIGATION. Synthetic engineering measurement only.**
